correctness.rationale: The source gives \(I_b^*=\mu_b(\mathcal R_0^b-1)/ eta_b\), so an all-positive equilibrium requires \(\mathcal R_0^b>1\). Under that condition and \( eta_{bh}>0\), the spillover pressure \(\kappa= eta_{bh}I_b^*\) is positive. Substitution of the source definition of \(\mathcal R_0^h\) reduces its human quadratic to one with positive leading coefficient and strictly negative constant term, forcing exactly one positive real root. Substituting that root into the source formulas makes \(S_h^*,E_h^*,R_h^*\) positive. The three \(\kappa\downarrow0\) limits follow by elementary expansion of the exact root and were replayed numerically.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 article prints the decisive quadratic but states the stronger and false feasibility condition requiring both reproduction numbers to exceed one. Source-specific searches on the DOI, endemic-equilibrium quadratic, subcritical human reproduction, and reservoir forcing located no correction. Earlier stochastic reservoir papers establish that spillover can matter below the incidental-host threshold, but they neither imply nor state the exact deterministic equilibrium root and crossover law for this eight-compartment avian-influenza system.
residual_risks: An unindexed correction or author note could already amend the motivating article's feasibility summary.
General reservoir-forcing phenomena are established prior art; novelty is limited to the exact deterministic source-specific correction and crossover formula.
No stability theorem for the forced positive equilibrium is claimed.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The corrected condition changes the epidemiological interpretation of a central equilibrium in a model designed to separate bird, zoonotic, and human transmission. Under endemic bird infection, a human reproduction number below one does not eliminate the positive human equilibrium; it only makes the equilibrium proportional to spillover at small forcing. The exact crossover quantifies how control of the bird reservoir and bird-to-human transmission can remain decisive even after autonomous human spread is subcritical, while preserving the source's valid disease-free result when both reproduction numbers are below one.
